output.brief: The wrong expiry dates were not caused by the agency operators or the printer firmware. Printer logs show that from 4 Oct 22:10, the data sent to the printers carried a 36-month shelf life instead of 24. This happened on all lines, including two Line 1 day-shift jobs run by permanent staff. No operator overrides occurred in any of the 47 jobs. The 30 jobs from June to 3 Oct, including those run after the firmware change, were correct. The ERP shows Regulatory Affairs entered 36 months on 3 Oct, but it is valid only from 1 Mar 2027, and the current value is still 24. So the line integration service appears to have read a future-dated value, which contradicts the vendor's claim. How it did so is not yet explained. Confidence is high on the cause and the timing. It is lower on whether other products are affected. Two other October edits, HX-15-30 and MR-05-14, have future dates and could behave the same way. Don't discipline the agency operators, and don't switch off the camera check. Do these now: fix the ERP shelf-life records, extend the hold to the two Line 1 Veltranol lots and any later Veltranol lots, and add a second-person check at each setup. Then inspect retained cartons of HX-15-30 and MR-05-14, and ask Corvane to explain how the future value got through.
